notes.title: Entity Selection Stick Is Still Active in Production
notes.problem: EntitySelectionLogger is initialized in the production Attack bootstrap. Any valid player using a normal minecraft:stick records coordinates and receives ctf_attack debug messages; sneaking with the stick removes/clears selections. The handler has no admin check.
notes.action: Remove EntitySelectionLogger from the release bootstrap, or gate the entire tool through the existing PermissionService admin owner. A normal gameplay item should not implicitly activate developer instrumentation.

evidence.finding: EntitySelectionLogger.init() subscribes to itemUse for minecraft:stick and is called unconditionally by the Attack bootstrap; addSelection() has no PermissionService check.

notes.title: World-Mutating Script Events Do Not Use the Existing Admin Permission Owner
notes.problem: Attack ships an explicit PermissionService, but GameManager script-event handlers for reset/force-start/force-end/skip-level and setup/reset services do not check PermissionService.isAdmin() before mutating session/world state. Command-level reachability may still restrict ordinary players, so this is not classified as an ordinary-player exploit from source alone.
notes.action: Route developer/admin script-event handlers through one explicit permission gate before performing world or session mutations. Do not rely only on external command reachability as the privilege boundary.

evidence.finding: GameManager receives ctf_attack reset/force/skip events and setup/reset services receive world-mutating script events without calling PermissionService.isAdmin().

notes.title: Admin Grant Secret Is Hard-Coded in the Shipped Behavior Script
notes.problem: permission.config embeds the admin grant/revoke secret directly in the distributed behavior script. Anyone with the world/add-on files can read the value, so it should not be treated as a durable secret boundary.
notes.action: Do not use a shipped static secret as the trust boundary. Prefer operator/host-controlled authorization or another runtime authority that is not recoverable from the distributed pack.

evidence.finding: permissionConfig contains a literal secretCode and PermissionService compares incoming set_admin/remove_admin messages against it.

notes.title: Attack Still Relies Heavily on Deprecated Async Command Calls
notes.problem: The v1.1.2 compiled behavior scripts contain 34 runCommandAsync() call sites. This is technical-debt/API-migration risk rather than a proven current gameplay failure.
notes.action: Migrate command-backed operations to supported direct APIs or the current command surface where practical, prioritizing lifecycle-critical inventory, ticking-area, setup, camera, and reset paths. Keep behavior parity while migrating.

evidence.finding: Full compiled-script scan counts 34 occurrences of runCommandAsync(): 22 in chunk-4L7PEIZ4.js, 6 in chunk-EJPDS27P.js, and 6 in chunk-UUF652QC.js.

notes.title: Daylight-Cycle GameRules Property Uses the Wrong Casing
notes.problem: WorldData still declares doDaylightCycle while the Script API GameRules property is doDayLightCycle, so setup cannot reliably reassert the intended daylight-cycle rule through that property owner.
notes.action: Correct the existing WorldData key to doDayLightCycle and keep WorldManager as the single setup owner.

notes.title: Drive Changelog Still Marks v1.1.1 as Current
notes.problem: The selected Drive folder now contains Attack Challenge v1.1.2.mcworld, but the adjacent Attack Challenge changelog still declares v1.1.1 as Current. This creates release-authority ambiguity even though the current world artifact and pack manifests identify v1.1.2.
notes.action: Update the Drive changelog so Current Version and Version History identify v1.1.2, and keep the current-world artifact as the release authority.

evidence.finding: Drive world filename is Attack Challenge v1.1.2.mcworld while the changelog text says Current Version v1.1.1 / v1.1.1 — Current.

notes.title: Kit Selection Immediately Refreshes Loadout Without a Gameplay-Phase Gate
notes.problem: KitManager accepts kit selection from its entity/script-event path and immediately reapplies the player's loadout. The handler does not check whether the arena is in buy_phase versus active combat. The in-arena kit structure contains the kit selector entities, so phase ownership should be explicit even though current source alone does not prove that players can reach/use those selectors during every active level.
notes.action: Make the intended kit-change window explicit. If kit changes are preparation-only, gate selection through the player's arena session status before applying a fresh loadout. If active-combat switching is intended, document it and preserve purchased-item handling deliberately.

evidence.finding: Kit selector interactions trigger kit selection; setSelectedKit() persists the selection and immediately calls applySelectedKitNow() with no session-phase check. kit.mcstructure contains kit-selector entities and is loaded once per enabled arena.

notes.title: Dedicated Shop-Item Preservation Helpers Are Dead Code
notes.problem: KitManager defines capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots() and restorePreservedShopItems(), and startBuyPhase carries a preservePersistentShopItems option, but the current production loadout path does not call those helpers. Actual survival of purchases relies on generic non-kit item displacement/preservation behavior instead.
notes.action: Remove the unused preservation path or connect one clear inventory-preservation owner. Avoid maintaining a named preservePersistentShopItems contract that is not actually consumed by applyPlayerLoadout().

evidence.finding: Full production-script search finds definitions of capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots()/restorePreservedShopItems() but no callers; applyPlayerLoadout() ignores preservePersistentShopItems and preserves non-kit items through clearKitManagedItems plus slot displacement.

notes.title: Kit Selection Has No Explicit Gameplay-Phase Gate
notes.problem: KitManager accepts kit selection and immediately reapplies the selected loadout whenever the selection event is reachable. The handler does not check whether the player's arena is in buy_phase versus active gameplay. Current artifact evidence does not establish that mid-combat selector reachability is intended or physically available on every level, so this is not promoted to a gameplay BUG.
notes.action: Define one explicit kit-change policy. If kit changes are preparation-only, enforce buy_phase at the KitManager owner; if live switching is intended, document it and preserve purchased-item/economy semantics deliberately.

evidence.finding: kit:select and kit-selector entity triggers call setSelectedKit(); setSelectedKit() persists the kit and calls applySelectedKitNow() without checking GameManager session phase.

notes.title: Dedicated Persistent-Shop-Item Preservation Helpers Are Not Used
notes.problem: KitManager contains capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots() and restorePreservedShopItems(), and startBuyPhase carries a preservePersistentShopItems option, but production search finds no call that uses those helpers to implement that option. Current purchased-item survival instead depends on clearing only kit-managed items and moving displaced non-kit items.
notes.action: Remove the dead preservation helpers/option if the slot-based policy is canonical, or connect them through one tested preservation owner. Keep the actual inventory contract explicit so future kit changes do not accidentally revive two competing preservation strategies.

evidence.finding: capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots() and restorePreservedShopItems() are defined but have no production callers; preservePersistentShopItems is passed through transition calls but not consumed by applyPlayerLoadout().

notes.title: Drive Changelog Still Identifies v1.1.1 as Current
notes.problem: The selected Drive world is Attack Challenge v1.1.2 and the BP/RP metadata are v1.1.2, but the Drive changelog still labels v1.1.1 as Current. This can misroute QA and version comparison even though the artifact itself is correctly versioned.
notes.action: Update the Drive changelog/current-version marker to v1.1.2 and keep artifact identity derived from the actual current world file rather than prose metadata.

evidence.finding: Drive folder contains Attack Challenge v1.1.2.mcworld uploaded 7 Oct 2026 while the fetched changelog still presents v1.1.1 as Current.
